paragraphs.text: I have one room available in a large apartment located just off Queen and Bathurst in Toronto. The room is fully furnished with a double bed, desk, shelf and wardrobe.
paragraphs.translation:
我在多伦多皇后街和巴瑟斯特街附近的一个大公寓里有一个房间可用。
房间家具齐全，配有一张双人床、书桌、架子和衣柜。

paragraphs.text: About us: 'm Sasha! I'm Canadian, and I've been living in this apartment since I was a teenager. I'm 23 and work in a restaurant. These past two years, my best friend has been living here but as she's now moving to Europe there is a room available as of October 1. The third room is occupied by Simon, who is from Australia. He works part-time in a music shop downtown and is a great drummer. We both like keeping the place neat and tidy - I actually enjoy cleaning in my spare time and sometimes we do it together as a roommate team (we make it fun!). I love watching movies, exploring, getting out of the city and into the outdoors, and listening to music.
paragraphs.translation:
关于我们：我是萨莎！
我是加拿大人，从青少年时期就一直住在这间公寓里。
我今年23岁，在一家餐厅工作。
过去两年里，我最好的朋友一直住在这里，但由于她现在要搬到欧洲去，从10月1日起会空出一间房。
第三个房间住着来自澳大利亚的西蒙。
他在市中心的一家音乐店兼职，还是一名出色的鼓手。
我们俩都喜欢保持住所整洁——我其实很享受在空闲时间打扫卫生，有时我们会作为室友团队一起做（我们把这件事变得有趣！）。
我喜欢看电影、探索事物、走出城市融入大自然，以及听音乐。

paragraphs.text: The apartment itself is very large and comes equipped with unlimited wi-fi, a fully stocked kitchen, cable television, and Netflix. The bedroom is a long way from the living room, so it shouldn't disturb you if people come round and besides, we are certainly very respectful. Oh! We also have two cats who are well-behaved but they might be a problem if you have allergies. If you have a pet, that's no problem - these cats get along with other animals.
paragraphs.translation:
公寓本身非常大，配备了无限Wi-Fi、储备齐全的厨房、有线电视和Netflix。
卧室距离客厅很远，所以即使有人来访也不会打扰到您，而且我们当然非常尊重他人。
哦！
我们还有两只行为良好的猫，但如果您有过敏症，它们可能会是个问题。
如果您有宠物，那也没问题——这些猫与其他动物相处融洽。

paragraphs.text: We love having people coming from other countries as it's really fun having the opportunity to show them around the neighborhood (it's a great neighborhood - lots of character and plenty to do). That said, we're certainly interested in living with Canadians too! We're very easy-going and open-minded and just hope that our new roommate will be the same.
paragraphs.translation:
我们喜欢接待来自其他国家的人，因为有机会带他们参观这个社区真的很有趣（这是一个很棒的社区——特色鲜明且活动丰富）。
话虽如此，我们也同样有兴趣与加拿大人同住！
我们非常随和且思想开放，只希望我们的新房客也能如此。

paragraphs.text: Smartphone fitness apps
paragraphs.translation: 智能手机健身应用程序

paragraphs.text: A Pacer
paragraphs.translation: 一款名为Pacer的应用程序

paragraphs.text: Although they were previously split into 'pro' and 'free' versions, Pacer's developer now generously includes all the features in one free app. That means you can spend no money, yet use your smartphone's GPS capabilities to track your jogging routes, and examine details of your pace and calories burned.
paragraphs.translation:
尽管此前该应用程序分为‘专业版’和‘免费版’，但Pacer的开发人员现在慷慨地将所有功能整合在一个免费应用中。
这意味着你无需花费任何费用，即可利用智能手机的GPS功能追踪你的慢跑路线，并查看你的步速和消耗卡路里的详细信息。

paragraphs.text: B Beat2
paragraphs.translation: B Beat2

paragraphs.text: There are a wealth of running apps available, but Beat2 is a good one. This free app monitors your pace - or if you have a wrist or chest-based heart rate monitor, your beats per minute - and offers up its specially curated playlists to give you the perfect music for the pace you're running at, adding a whole new dimension to your run. The best bit is when you explode into a sprint and the music pounds in your ears. Or if you fancy something different, the app also has In-App Purchases, including tales of past sporting heroes you can listen to while you run.
paragraphs.translation:
有大量可用的跑步应用程序，但 Beat2 是一款不错的产品。
这款免费应用会监测你的步速——或者如果你有腕式或胸式心率监测器，还会监测你每分钟的心跳——并提供其精心策划的播放列表，为你跑步时的步速匹配完美的音乐，为你的跑步增添一个全新的维度。
最棒的部分是当你猛然加速冲刺时，音乐在耳中轰鸣作响。
或者，如果你喜欢不同的内容，该应用还提供应用内购买项目，包括你可以边跑步边聆听的昔日体育英雄的故事。

paragraphs.text: C Impel
paragraphs.translation: C Impel 应用程序

paragraphs.text: If you're serious about the sport you do, then you should be serious about Impel. As smartphone fitness tools go it's one of the best, allowing you to track your performance, set goals and see daily progress updates. If you're ever not sure where to run or cycle you can find user-created routes on the app, or share your own. All of that comes free of charge, while a premium version adds even more tools.
paragraphs.translation:
如果你认真对待你所从事的运动，那么你也应该认真对待 Impel。
作为智能手机健身工具，它是最好的之一，让你可以追踪自己的表现、设定目标并查看每日进度更新。
如果你不确定在哪里跑步或骑行，可以在应用上找到用户创建的路线，或分享你自己的路线。
所有这些都免费提供，而高级版本则增加了更多工具。

paragraphs.text: D Fast Track
paragraphs.translation: D 快速追踪

paragraphs.text: There are plenty of GPS running apps for smartphones, but Fast Track is an excellent freebie. Although you naturally get more features if you pay for the 'pro' version, the free release gets you GPS tracking, a nicely designed map view, your training history, music, and cheering. Yes, you read the last of those right - you can have friends cheer you on as you huff and puff during a run. If you can afford the 'pro' version, you can add possible routes, voice coaches, smartwatch connectivity and more; but as a starting point, the free app gets you moving.
paragraphs.translation:
智能手机上有很多GPS跑步应用程序，但快速追踪是个出色的免费应用。
虽然付费购买专业版自然能获得更多功能，但免费版本也能提供GPS追踪、设计精美的地图视图、训练历史、音乐和加油助威功能。
是的，你没看错最后一项——你可以让朋友在你跑步气喘吁吁时为你加油打气。
如果你负担得起专业版，还能添加可能的路线、语音教练、智能手表连接等功能；但作为起点，免费应用就能让你动起来。

groups.instructions:

Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information given in the text, choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt: The room available has two beds.
questions.analysis: 题干称“available room has two beds”（房间有两张床），但原文明确指出“The room is fully furnished with a double bed...”，其中“double bed”指的是一张双人床，而非两张单人床。因此，题干信息与原文矛盾，答案为 FALSE。
questions.reason: 原句明确 only a double bed，非 two beds。
questions.location_analysis: 原文说 double bed（双人床）是一张，不是两张，所以 FALSE。
questions.paraphrasing: two beds -> double bed
evidence: The room is fully furnished with a double bed, desk, shelf and wardrobe.

wrong_reasons.TRUE: 原文中明确提到了床的数量，与题干中的两张床不一致。
wrong_reasons.NOT GIVEN: 原文已经明确给出了床的数量信息，因此不能选未提及。

questions.prompt: The Australian in Sasha's apartment is a musician.
questions.analysis: 题干询问“澳大利亚室友是否是音乐人”。原文提到“The third room is occupied by Simon, who is from Australia... and is a great drummer”，而鼓手（drummer）属于音乐人（musician）的一种。因此，题干与原文信息一致，答案为 TRUE。
questions.location_analysis: Simon from Australia 是 drummer（鼓手），即 musician。
questions.paraphrasing: Australian -> from Australia; musician -> great drummer
evidence: The third room is occupied by Simon, who is from Australia. He works part-time in a music shop downtown and is a great drummer.

wrong_reasons.FALSE: 与原文信息矛盾，原文明确指出这位澳大利亚人是音乐家。
wrong_reasons.NOT GIVEN: 原文已明确给出该信息，并非未提及。

questions.prompt: Sasha does all the cleaning in the apartment.
questions.analysis: 题干声称“Sasha 独自完成所有清洁工作”，但原文写道“I actually enjoy cleaning in my spare time and sometimes we do it together as a roommate team”，说明清洁是 Sasha 和室友共同完成的，并非她一人包办。因此，题干与原文不符，答案为 FALSE。
questions.reason: 原文提到一起做，故说 Sasha 全做 FALSE。
questions.location_analysis: Sasha 喜欢打扫，但有时与室友一起做，并非独自一人。
questions.paraphrasing: all the cleaning -> I actually enjoy cleaning... sometimes we do it together
evidence: I actually enjoy cleaning in my spare time and sometimes we do it together as a roommate team (we make it fun!).

wrong_reasons.TRUE: 与原文信息矛盾（原文表明Sasha并未承担全部清洁工作）。
wrong_reasons.NOT GIVEN: 原文已明确给出相关信息（Sasha未做全部清洁），并非未提及。

questions.prompt: Sasha likes being in the open air.
questions.analysis: 题干说“Sasha 喜欢在户外活动”，原文中 Sasha 明确表示“I love... getting out of the city and into the outdoors”，其中“outdoors”即指开放的自然环境，与“open air”含义一致。因此，题干与原文相符，答案为 TRUE。
questions.reason: 原文直接提及喜欢户外。
questions.location_analysis: Sasha喜欢户外活动，原文明确提到‘getting out of the city and...
questions.paraphrasing: open air -> outdoors
evidence: I love watching movies, exploring, getting out of the city and into the outdoors, and listening to music.

wrong_reasons.FALSE: 该选项与题干意思相反，题干明确表示Sasha喜欢户外。
wrong_reasons.NOT GIVEN: 题干已明确给出信息，因此该选项不正确。

questions.prompt: The room available would be suitable for someone who likes to be quiet.
questions.analysis: 题干认为“该房间适合喜欢安静的人”。原文提到“The bedroom is a long way from the living room, so it shouldn't disturb you if people come round”，说明卧室位置远离公共区域，不易被打扰，且室友“very respectful”，进一步支持安静的居住环境。因此答案为 TRUE。
questions.reason: 原文说明卧室安静，适合喜欢安静的人。
questions.location_analysis: 卧室远离客厅，安静不被打扰。
questions.paraphrasing: like to be quiet -> shouldn't disturb you if people come round
evidence: The bedroom is a long way from the living room, so it shouldn't disturb you if people come round and besides, we are certainly very respectful.

wrong_reasons.FALSE: 原文明确说明房间适合喜欢安静的人，与题干一致，因此该选项错误。
wrong_reasons.NOT GIVEN: 原文已直接提供信息，该选项错误，因为题干内容在原文中有明确依据。

questions.prompt: Sasha thinks her apartment is in the best part of Toronto.
questions.analysis: 题干称“Sasha 认为她的公寓位于多伦多最好的区域”，但原文仅说“it's a great neighborhood - lots of character and plenty to do”，并未使用最高级“best”或进行比较，无法推断她认为这是“最好”的地方。因此信息未提及，答案为 NOT GIVEN。

questions.location_analysis: 原文只说街区很有特色，但未说最佳区域，NOT GIVEN。
questions.paraphrasing: best part -> (未提及)
evidence: it's a great neighborhood - lots of character and plenty to do

wrong_reasons.TRUE: 原文未提及Sasha认为她的公寓在多伦多最好的区域，属于无中生有。
wrong_reasons.FALSE: 原文没有信息表明Sasha不认为她的公寓在多伦多最好的区域，因此不能判断为错误。

questions.prompt: Sasha has never had a roommate from Canada.
questions.analysis: 题干称“Sasha 从未有过加拿大籍室友”，但原文只说“We're certainly interested in living with Canadians too!”，这表明她对与加拿大人合住持开放态度，但并未说明过去是否有过此类经历。因此该信息在文中未给出，答案为 NOT GIVEN。
questions.reason: 原文未提供关于过去室友国籍的信息。
questions.location_analysis: 原文说也对加拿大人感兴趣，但未说明过去有无，NOT GIVEN。
questions.paraphrasing: never had -> interested in living with Canadians too (暗示可能有或可能没有)
questions.keywords: never had a roommate from Canada
evidence: That said, we're certainly interested in living with Canadians too!

wrong_reasons.TRUE: 原文未提及Sasha是否有过加拿大室友，无法确认该陈述正确。
wrong_reasons.FALSE: 原文未提及Sasha有过加拿大室友，无法确认该陈述错误。

questions.paraphrasing: well-presented visuals -> a nicely designed map view

questions.prompt: You do not have to pay for any of the features on this app.

questions.location_analysis: A 段说明所有功能免费整合在 free app。

questions.keywords: do not have to pay, any of the features

questions.prompt: You can pay to download true stories on this app.

questions.location_analysis: B 段有付费购买体育英雄故事的功能。

evidence: Or if you fancy something different, the app also has In-App Purchases, including tales of past sporting heroes you can listen to while you run.

questions.prompt: You can get ideas about where to go from other people on this app.
questions.analysis: 题干询问哪款应用能“从他人那里获得去哪里的建议”。C 段（Impel）指出用户可“find user-created routes on the app”，即查看其他用户创建的路线，这正是从他人获取出行建议的方式，因此答案为 C。
questions.reason: 用户创建路线即从他人获取想法。
questions.location_analysis: C 段提到可查看他人创建的路线。
questions.paraphrasing: ideas from other people -> user-created routes
evidence: If you're ever not sure where to run or cycle you can find user-created routes on the app, or share your own.

questions.prompt: This app gives you details of the energy you have used.
questions.analysis: 题干要求找出提供“能量消耗详情”的应用。A 段（Pacer）提到可“examine details of your pace and calories burned”，其中“calories burned”即身体消耗的能量，与“energy you have used”含义一致，因此答案为 A。
questions.reason: calories burned 对应 energy used。
questions.location_analysis: A 段提到追踪卡路里（calories burned）即能量消耗。
questions.paraphrasing: energy used -> calories burned
evidence: That means you can spend no money, yet use your smartphone's GPS capabilities to track your jogging routes, and examine details of your pace and calories burned.

parts.title: Passage 2
parts.article_title: Why You Should Delegate Tasks to Team Members

paragraphs.text: Delegation helps you get more done, helps your team members progress through learning new things and spreads the load in the team.
paragraphs.translation: 委派任务能帮助你完成更多工作，通过让团队成员学习新事物来促进他们的进步，并分散团队的工作负担。

paragraphs.text: When you give someone a project task to do, make sure that they have all the information they require to actually get on and do it. That includes specifying the date it is due, writing a clear definition of the task, providing any resources they need to get it done or names of people you expect them to talk to. It also means informing them of any expectations you have, such as delivering it as a spreadsheet rather than a Word document.
paragraphs.translation:
当你将某个项目任务分配给某人时，务必确保他们拥有实际着手执行该任务所需的所有信息。
这包括明确截止日期、撰写清晰的任务描述、提供他们完成任务所需的任何资源，或者列出你期望他们与之沟通的人员姓名。
这也意味着告知他们你所持有的任何期望，例如以电子表格而非Word文档的形式提交成果。

paragraphs.text: If you have concerns that someone doesn't have the skills to do a good job(or they tell you this outright), make sure that you offer some help. It might take longer this time but next time they will be able to do it without you, so it will save you time in the long run.
paragraphs.translation:
如果你担心某人不具备做好工作的技能（或者他们直接告诉你这一点），请确保提供一些帮助。
这次可能会花费更长时间，但下次他们就能在没有你的情况下完成任务，因此从长远来看会为你节省时间。

paragraphs.text: Once you have given the task to someone, let them get on with it. Tell them how you expect to be kept informed, like through a report once a week. Then let them get on with it, unless you feel things are not progressing as you would like.
paragraphs.translation:
一旦你把任务交给了某人，就让他们自行完成。
告知他们你希望如何了解进展，例如通过每周一次的报告。
然后让他们继续工作，除非你觉得事情的进展不如你所愿。

paragraphs.text: As a project manager, you have to retain some of the main project responsibilities for yourself. You shouldn’t expect someone else on the project team to do your job. Equally, don't delegate tasks such as dull administrative ones, just because you don't want to do them. But remember that project management is a leadership position so you don't want your role to be seen as too basic.
paragraphs.translation:
作为项目经理，你必须将一些主要的项目职责留给自己。
你不应指望项目团队中的其他人来做你的工作。
同样地，不要仅仅因为自己不想做，就委派那些枯燥的行政类任务。
但请记住，项目管理是一个领导职位，所以你不希望自己的角色被视为过于基础。

paragraphs.text: One way to free up your time to spend on the more strategic and leadership parts of project management is to delegate things that are regular, like noting whether weekly targets have been met. Could someone in your team take this on for you? This can be a useful way of upskilling your team members to complement any ongoing training and allowing them to gain confidence too.
paragraphs.translation:
一种释放时间以专注于项目管理中更具战略性和领导力方面的方法，是将常规事务委托给他人，例如记录每周目标是否已完成。
你团队中的某个人能否为你承担这项任务？
这可能是提升团队成员技能的一种有用方式，既补充了任何持续的培训，也让他们获得信心。

paragraphs.text: So in summary, be clear, supportive, and don't micromanage. Don't become the problem on your project that prevents progress just because you're afraid to leave people alone to get on with their jobs.
paragraphs.translation:
总之，要清晰、支持，并且不要微观管理。
不要因为你害怕让员工独自完成工作，而成为阻碍项目进展的问题。

paragraphs.text: Choosing the right format for your CV
paragraphs.translation: 为你的简历选择正确的格式

paragraphs.text: A good CV should be clear, simple and easy to understand. Here are four of the most popular CV formats and advice on when to use them:
paragraphs.translation:
一份好的简历应当清晰、简洁且易于理解。
以下是四种最流行的简历格式以及关于何时使用它们的建议：

paragraphs.text: Chronological
paragraphs.translation: 按时间顺序排列

paragraphs.text: This is the traditional CV format and is extremely popular because it allows employers to see all the posts you have held in order. It provides flexibility because it works in almost all circumstances, the exception being if you have blocks of unemployment that are difficult to account for. This type of format is particularly useful when you have a solid and complete working history spanning five years or more.
paragraphs.translation:
这是传统的简历格式，非常受欢迎，因为它能让雇主按顺序看到你所担任的所有职位。
它提供了灵活性，因为几乎适用于所有情况，唯一的例外是当你有一段难以解释的失业空白期时。
这种格式在你拥有连续且完整的五年以上工作经历时尤其有用。

paragraphs.text: Functional
paragraphs.translation: 功能性简历

paragraphs.text: The functional CV is designed to describe your key skills rather than the jobs you have done. The functional CV format is typically used by people who have extensive gaps in their employment history, or have often changed jobs. It also suits those who want to go in a different direction work-wise and change industry. You might choose it if you want to highlight skills learned early in your career, points that might get missed if a chronological format is used. It is also appropriate if you have done little or no actual work, for example, if you are one of the current year's graduates.
paragraphs.translation:
按时间顺序排列
功能性简历
功能性简历旨在描述你的关键技能，而非你曾从事过的工作。
功能性简历格式通常被那些工作经历中有长时间空档或频繁更换工作的人所使用。
它也适合那些希望在职业方向上另辟蹊径并转换行业的人。
如果你希望突出在职业生涯早期学到的技能（这些要点在使用按时间顺序的简历格式时可能会被忽略），你可以选择这种格式。
如果你几乎没有实际工作经验，例如你是应届毕业生，这种格式也很合适。

paragraphs.text: Because this format is often used to cover a patchy employment history, some interviewers may view such CVs with suspicion, so be very careful should you choose it.
paragraphs.translation: 由于这种格式常被用来掩盖不连贯的工作经历，一些面试官可能会对此类简历持怀疑态度，因此如果你选择它，务必格外谨慎。

paragraphs.text: Achievement
paragraphs.translation: 成就

paragraphs.text: An alternative to the functional CV is to use an achievement-based résumé highlighting key achievements in place of skills. This can help show your suitability for a role if you lack direct experience of it.
paragraphs.translation:
功能性简历
成就
功能型简历的另一种选择是使用以成就为基础的简历，突出关键成就而非技能。
如果你缺乏某个角色的直接经验，这有助于展示你对该职位的适合性。

paragraphs.text: Non-traditional
paragraphs.translation: 非传统型

paragraphs.text: With the explosion of digital and creative industries over recent years, CV formats have become more and more imaginative. You can present information through graphics, which can be more visually engaging and turn out to be an unusual but winning option. This will definitely make you stand out from the crowd. It also demonstrates design skills and creativity in a way that a potential employer can see and feel. However, a highly creative CV format is only really appropriate for creative and artistic sectors, such as those involving promoting products, though it would also work for the media too.
paragraphs.translation:
随着近年来数字和创意产业的蓬勃发展，简历格式变得越来越富有想象力。
你可以通过图形来呈现信息，这种方式在视觉上更具吸引力，并可能成为一种不寻常但成功的选项。
这无疑会使你从众人中脱颖而出。
它还能以一种潜在雇主看得见、感受得到的方式展示设计技能和创造力。
然而，高度创意的简历格式仅真正适用于创意和艺术领域，例如涉及产品推广的行业，尽管它同样适用于媒体行业。

parts.source_article_title: Why You Should Delegate Tasks to Team Members

sentence_translations.sentence: Delegation helps you get more done, helps your team members progress through learning new things and spreads the load in the team.
sentence_translations.translation: 委派任务能帮助你完成更多工作，通过让团队成员学习新事物来促进他们的进步，并分散团队的工作负担。

sentence_translations.sentence: When you give someone a project task to do, make sure that they have all the information they require to actually get on and do it.
sentence_translations.translation: 当你将某个项目任务分配给某人时，务必确保他们拥有实际着手执行该任务所需的所有信息。

sentence_translations.sentence: That includes specifying the date it is due, writing a clear definition of the task, providing any resources they need to get it done or names of people you expect them to talk to.
sentence_translations.translation: 这包括明确截止日期、撰写清晰的任务描述、提供他们完成任务所需的任何资源，或者列出你期望他们与之沟通的人员姓名。

sentence_translations.sentence: It also means informing them of any expectations you have, such as delivering it as a spreadsheet rather than a Word document.
sentence_translations.translation: 这也意味着告知他们你所持有的任何期望，例如以电子表格而非Word文档的形式提交成果。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you have concerns that someone doesn't have the skills to do a good job(or they tell you this outright), make sure that you offer some help.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你担心某人不具备做好工作的技能（或者他们直接告诉你这一点），请确保提供一些帮助。

sentence_translations.sentence: It might take longer this time but next time they will be able to do it without you, so it will save you time in the long run.
sentence_translations.translation: 这次可能会花费更长时间，但下次他们就能在没有你的情况下完成任务，因此从长远来看会为你节省时间。

sentence_translations.sentence: Once you have given the task to someone, let them get on with it.
sentence_translations.translation: 一旦你把任务交给了某人，就让他们自行完成。

sentence_translations.sentence: Tell them how you expect to be kept informed, like through a report once a week.
sentence_translations.translation: 告知他们你希望如何了解进展，例如通过每周一次的报告。

sentence_translations.sentence: Then let them get on with it, unless you feel things are not progressing as you would like.
sentence_translations.translation: 然后让他们继续工作，除非你觉得事情的进展不如你所愿。

sentence_translations.sentence: As a project manager, you have to retain some of the main project responsibilities for yourself.
sentence_translations.translation: 作为项目经理，你必须将一些主要的项目职责留给自己。

sentence_translations.sentence: You shouldn’t expect someone else on the project team to do your job.
sentence_translations.translation: 你不应指望项目团队中的其他人来做你的工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: Equally, don't delegate tasks such as dull administrative ones, just because you don't want to do them.
sentence_translations.translation: 同样地，不要仅仅因为自己不想做，就委派那些枯燥的行政类任务。

sentence_translations.sentence: But remember that project management is a leadership position so you don't want your role to be seen as too basic.
sentence_translations.translation: 但请记住，项目管理是一个领导职位，所以你不希望自己的角色被视为过于基础。

sentence_translations.sentence: One way to free up your time to spend on the more strategic and leadership parts of project management is to delegate things that are regular, like noting whether weekly targets have been met.
sentence_translations.translation: 一种释放时间以专注于项目管理中更具战略性和领导力方面的方法，是将常规事务委托给他人，例如记录每周目标是否已完成。

sentence_translations.sentence: Could someone in your team take this on for you?
sentence_translations.translation: 你团队中的某个人能否为你承担这项任务？

sentence_translations.sentence: This can be a useful way of upskilling your team members to complement any ongoing training and allowing them to gain confidence too.
sentence_translations.translation: 这可能是提升团队成员技能的一种有用方式，既补充了任何持续的培训，也让他们获得信心。

sentence_translations.sentence: So in summary, be clear, supportive, and don't micromanage.
sentence_translations.translation: 总之，要清晰、支持，并且不要微观管理。

sentence_translations.sentence: Don't become the problem on your project that prevents progress just because you're afraid to leave people alone to get on with their jobs.
sentence_translations.translation: 不要因为你害怕让员工独自完成工作，而成为阻碍项目进展的问题。

sentence_translations.sentence: Choosing the right format for your CV
sentence_translations.translation: 为你的简历选择正确的格式

sentence_translations.sentence: A good CV should be clear, simple and easy to understand.
sentence_translations.translation: 一份好的简历应当清晰、简洁且易于理解。

sentence_translations.sentence: Here are four of the most popular CV formats and advice on when to use them:
sentence_translations.translation: 以下是四种最流行的简历格式以及关于何时使用它们的建议：

sentence_translations.sentence: Chronological
sentence_translations.translation: 按时间顺序排列

sentence_translations.sentence: This is the traditional CV format and is extremely popular because it allows employers to see all the posts you have held in order.
sentence_translations.translation: 这是传统的简历格式，非常受欢迎，因为它能让雇主按顺序看到你所担任的所有职位。

sentence_translations.sentence: It provides flexibility because it works in almost all circumstances, the exception being if you have blocks of unemployment that are difficult to account for.
sentence_translations.translation: 它提供了灵活性，因为几乎适用于所有情况，唯一的例外是当你有一段难以解释的失业空白期时。

sentence_translations.sentence: This type of format is particularly useful when you have a solid and complete working history spanning five years or more.
sentence_translations.translation: 这种格式在你拥有连续且完整的五年以上工作经历时尤其有用。

sentence_translations.sentence: Functional
sentence_translations.translation: 功能性简历

sentence_translations.sentence: The functional CV is designed to describe your key skills rather than the jobs you have done.
sentence_translations.translation: 功能性简历旨在描述你的关键技能，而非你曾从事过的工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: The functional CV format is typically used by people who have extensive gaps in their employment history, or have often changed jobs.
sentence_translations.translation: 功能性简历格式通常被那些工作经历中有长时间空档或频繁更换工作的人所使用。

sentence_translations.sentence: It also suits those who want to go in a different direction work-wise and change industry.
sentence_translations.translation: 它也适合那些希望在职业方向上另辟蹊径并转换行业的人。

sentence_translations.sentence: You might choose it if you want to highlight skills learned early in your career, points that might get missed if a chronological format is used.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你希望突出在职业生涯早期学到的技能（这些要点在使用按时间顺序的简历格式时可能会被忽略），你可以选择这种格式。

sentence_translations.sentence: It is also appropriate if you have done little or no actual work, for example, if you are one of the current year's graduates.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你几乎没有实际工作经验，例如你是应届毕业生，这种格式也很合适。

sentence_translations.sentence: Because this format is often used to cover a patchy employment history, some interviewers may view such CVs with suspicion, so be very careful should you choose it.
sentence_translations.translation: 由于这种格式常被用来掩盖不连贯的工作经历，一些面试官可能会对此类简历持怀疑态度，因此如果你选择它，务必格外谨慎。

sentence_translations.sentence: Achievement
sentence_translations.translation: 成就

sentence_translations.sentence: An alternative to the functional CV is to use an achievement-based résumé highlighting key achievements in place of skills.
sentence_translations.translation: 功能型简历的另一种选择是使用以成就为基础的简历，突出关键成就而非技能。

sentence_translations.sentence: This can help show your suitability for a role if you lack direct experience of it.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你缺乏某个角色的直接经验，这有助于展示你对该职位的适合性。

sentence_translations.sentence: Non-traditional
sentence_translations.translation: 非传统型

sentence_translations.sentence: With the explosion of digital and creative industries over recent years, CV formats have become more and more imaginative.
sentence_translations.translation: 随着近年来数字和创意产业的蓬勃发展，简历格式变得越来越富有想象力。

sentence_translations.sentence: You can present information through graphics, which can be more visually engaging and turn out to be an unusual but winning option.
sentence_translations.translation: 你可以通过图形来呈现信息，这种方式在视觉上更具吸引力，并可能成为一种不寻常但成功的选项。

sentence_translations.sentence: This will definitely make you stand out from the crowd.
sentence_translations.translation: 这无疑会使你从众人中脱颖而出。

sentence_translations.sentence: It also demonstrates design skills and creativity in a way that a potential employer can see and feel.
sentence_translations.translation: 它还能以一种潜在雇主看得见、感受得到的方式展示设计技能和创造力。

sentence_translations.sentence: However, a highly creative CV format is only really appropriate for creative and artistic sectors, such as those involving promoting products, though it would also work for the media too.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，高度创意的简历格式仅真正适用于创意和艺术领域，例如涉及产品推广的行业，尽管它同样适用于媒体行业。

parts.title: Passage 3
parts.article_title: DINOSAURS AND THE SECRETS THEY STILL HOLD

paragraphs.text: Dinosaur expert Dr Steve Brusatte continues to investigate the mysteries surrounding these fascinating prehistoric creatures
paragraphs.translation: 恐龙专家史蒂夫·布鲁萨特博士继续探究这些迷人史前生物所围绕的谜团。

paragraphs.text: A

I was recently part of a team of palaeontologists that discovered a new dinosaur. Living in what is now China, the species would have resembled a strange bird. It was about the size of a sheep and covered in feathers, with a sharp beak that it probably used to crack open shellfish. It was given the formal scientific name Tongtianlong, but we called it ‘Mud Dragon’ because its skeleton was discovered in rock that had hardened from ancient mud. It seems that the creature got trapped in the mud and died. Then its fossil remains were found a few months ago when workmen were excavating a site in order to build a school.
paragraphs.translation:
我最近加入了一个古生物学家团队，发现了一种新的恐龙。
这种物种生活在现在的中国地区，外形类似一种奇特的鸟类。
它大约有羊那么大，全身覆盖着羽毛，长着锋利的喙，可能用来敲开贝类。
它的正式科学名称是‘通天龙’，但我们称它为‘泥浆龙’，因为它的骨骼是在由古代泥浆硬化而成的岩石中发现的。
这只生物似乎被困在泥浆中并死亡了。
随后，几个月前工人们在挖掘一个工地以建造学校时，发现了它的化石遗骸。

paragraphs.text: B

It is every dinosaur-obsessed child's dearest wish to discover and name a completely new species. In fact what my colleagues and I did wasn't that unusual. New dinosaurs are appearing everywhere these days – about 50 each year. And this pace shows no signs of slowing, as different areas continue to open up to fossil hunters and a fresh generation of scientists comes of age. Because of this plentiful supply of new fossils, we now know more about dinosaurs than we do about many modern animals. But there are still many unsolved mysteries.
paragraphs.translation:
每个痴迷恐龙的孩子最渴望的就是发现并命名一个全新的物种。
事实上，我和我的同事们所做的并不那么罕见。
如今，新恐龙物种层出不穷——每年大约有50种被发现。
而且这一速度毫无放缓迹象，因为不同地区不断向化石猎人开放，新一代科学家也日渐成熟。
由于新化石的大量涌现，我们现在对恐龙的了解甚至超过了许多现代动物。
但仍有许多未解之谜。

paragraphs.text: C

Dinosaurs didn't start out as huge monsters like Tyrannosaurus Rex. Instead they evolved from a group of angular, cat-sized reptiles called dinosauromorphs. These creatures remained small and rare for millions of years until they developed into dinosaurs. The boundary between dinosauromorphs and dinosaurs is becoming less and less distinct with each new discovery that's made, but what's becoming clear is that it took millions of years for these first dinosaurs to spread around the world, grow to huge sizes and become truly dominant.
paragraphs.translation:
恐龙一开始并非像霸王龙那样的巨型怪兽。
相反，它们是从一群体型如猫、棱角分明的爬行动物——恐龙形态类——进化而来的。
这些生物在数百万年间始终保持体型小且数量稀少，直到它们进化成恐龙。
随着每一项新发现，恐龙形态类与恐龙之间的界限正变得越来越模糊，但逐渐清晰的是，这些最早的恐龙花费了数百万年才扩散到世界各地，长成巨大体型并真正成为统治物种。

paragraphs.text: D

Some discoveries in the 1970s, like the agile and strangely bird-like Deinonychus, proved that dinosaurs were far more dynamic and intelligent than previously thought. Some palaeontologists even proposed that they were warm-blooded creatures like modern birds with a constant high body temperature that they controlled internally, rather than from warming themselves by lying in the sun. A few decades later opinions are still mixed. The problem is that dinosaurs can't be observed. Palaeontologists must rely on studying fossils. Some results are convincing: we know from studying their bones that dinosaurs had rapid growth rates, just like modern, warm-blooded animals. Other palaeontologists, however, use the same fossils to suggest that dinosaurs were somewhere between cold-blooded reptiles and warm-blooded birds. More studies are needed to provide more clarity.
paragraphs.translation:
20世纪70年代的一些发现，例如敏捷且异常像鸟类的恐爪龙，证明恐龙比先前认为的要更加活跃、更为聪明。
一些古生物学家甚至提出，它们是类似现代鸟类的温血动物，通过内部调节保持恒定的高体温，而非依靠晒太阳来取暖。
几十年后，观点仍存在分歧。
问题在于恐龙无法被直接观察。
古生物学家必须依赖研究化石。
有些结果是令人信服的：通过研究它们的骨骼，我们得知恐龙的生长速度很快，就像现代温血动物一样。
然而，其他古生物学家利用同样的化石提出，恐龙介于冷血爬行动物和温血鸟类之间。
需要更多研究来提供更清晰的结论。

paragraphs.text: E

The discovery of Deinonychus with its long arms, skinny legs, arched neck and big claws on its feet, helped to strengthen the theory that birds evolved from dinosaurs. In the late 1990s, the discovery of thousands of feather-covered dinosaurs closed the argument. But the fossils raised another question: why did feathers first develop in dinosaurs? They probably originated as simple, hair-like strands - a necessary means of keeping warm. Many dinosaurs retained this basic fluffy coat, but in one group the strands modified. They grew bigger, started to branch out and changed into feathers like those on modern birds. They lined the arms, and sometimes the legs, forming wings. These feathers were probably for display: to attract mates or scare off rivals. They appeared in species such as the ostrich-like Ornithomimosaur. Such creatures were too large to fly. Flight may actually have come about by accident when smaller winged dinosaurs began jumping between trees or leaping in the air, and suddenly found that their wings had aerodynamic properties. This is one of the most stimulating new notions about dinosaurs and a fascinating area for further investigation.
paragraphs.translation:
发现拥有长手臂、细腿、弓形脖子和脚上大爪子的恐爪龙，加强了鸟类由恐龙进化而来的理论。
在20世纪90年代末，数千具覆盖羽毛的恐龙的发现结束了这场争论。
但这些化石提出了另一个问题：恐龙最初为何会进化出羽毛？
它们可能最初是简单的毛发状纤维——一种必要的保暖方式。
许多恐龙保留了这种基本的蓬松外衣，但在一个群体中，这些纤维发生了改变。
它们变得更大，开始分叉，并演变成类似于现代鸟类的羽毛。
它们排列在手臂上，有时也在腿上，形成了翅膀。
这些羽毛可能用于展示：以吸引配偶或吓退竞争对手。
它们出现在诸如类似鸵鸟的似鸟龙等物种中。
这些生物体型过大，无法飞行。
飞行实际上可能源于偶然，当较小的有翼恐龙开始在林间跳跃或空中腾跃时，突然发现它们的翅膀具有空气动力学特性。
这是关于恐龙最令人振奋的新观念之一，也是一个值得进一步研究的迷人领域。

paragraphs.text: F

There's something else that these feathers can tell us. They allow us to determine what colour dinosaurs were. If you look at modern bird feathers under a microscope, you can see tiny blobs called melanosomes. These structures contain melanin, one of the main colour-producing pigments in animals. Some are round, others are egg-shaped, etc. And that's important, because different shapes contain different colour pigments. So if you can identify the shape, you can identify the colour. A few years ago, some palaeontologists realised that you could find melanosomes in particularly well-preserved fossil feathers. They discovered that different dinosaurs had different melanosomes, which meant they had a variety of colours. Dinosaurs, therefore, probably came in a rainbow of colours - yet another thing that links them to modern birds.
paragraphs.translation:
这些羽毛还能告诉我们一些别的事情。
它们使我们能够确定恐龙的颜色。
如果你在显微镜下观察现代鸟类的羽毛，你会看到称为黑色素体的小点。
这些结构含有黑色素，这是动物体内产生颜色的主要色素之一。
有些是圆形的，其他的则是蛋形的，等等。
这很重要，因为不同的形状含有不同的颜色色素。
所以如果你能辨别形状，你就能辨别颜色。
几年前，一些古生物学家意识到你可以在保存特别完好的化石羽毛中找到黑色素体。
他们发现不同的恐龙拥有不同的黑色素体，这意味着它们有各种各样的颜色。
因此，恐龙很可能呈现五彩斑斓的颜色——这又是将它们与现代鸟类联系起来的另一个特征。

paragraphs.text: G

The most enduring mystery of all, which has been argued about ever since the first dinosaur fossils were found, is ‘Why aren't dinosaurs around today?' Of course, we now know that birds evolved from dinosaurs, so some dinosaurs do continue in a sense. But there's nothing like a Tyrannosaurus Rex today. They dominated the planet for over 150 million years, but suddenly disappeared from the fossil record 66 million years ago. That's when a 10 km-wide asteroid came out of space and struck what is now Mexico, impacting with huge force and unleashing earthquakes, tidal waves, wildfires and hurricane-force winds. Although palaeontologists still like to argue about what part the asteroid played in the dinosaurs’ extinction, there really isn't much of a mystery left. The asteroid did it and did it quickly. There are few signs that dinosaurs were struggling before the impact. None survived except a few birds and some small furry mammals. They found themselves in an empty world, and as the planet started to recover, they evolved into new creatures, including the first apes, and so the long journey began to the beginning of humankind.
paragraphs.translation:
当然，我们现在知道鸟类是从恐龙进化而来的，所以从某种意义上说，一些恐龙确实延续了下来。
但今天再也没有像霸王龙那样的生物了。
它们统治地球超过1.5亿年，却在6600万年前突然从化石记录中消失。
那时，一颗宽达10公里的小行星从太空飞来，撞击了现在的墨西哥地区，造成巨大冲击，引发了地震、海啸、野火和飓风级强风。
尽管古生物学家仍喜欢争论小行星在恐龙灭绝中起到了多大作用，但实际上已经没有什么谜团了。
小行星造成了这一切，而且发生得很快。
几乎没有迹象表明恐龙在撞击前已经处于困境。
除了少数鸟类和一些小型毛茸茸的哺乳动物外，没有其他生物幸存下来。
它们发现自己身处一个空旷的世界，随着地球开始恢复，它们进化成了新的生物，包括最早的猿类，由此开启了通向人类起源的漫长旅程。
所有谜题中最经久不衰的一个，自第一块恐龙化石被发现以来就一直争论不休，那就是‘为什么恐龙如今不再存在了？’
但如今已经没有像霸王龙这样的生物了。
那时，一颗宽10公里的小行星从太空而来，撞击了现在的墨西哥地区，产生了巨大的冲击力，引发了地震、海啸、野火和飓风级的大风。
尽管古生物学家仍然喜欢争论小行星在恐龙灭绝中扮演了什么角色，但实际上已经没有太多谜团了。
是小行星造成了这一切，并且速度很快。

parts.source_article_title: DINOSAURS AND THE SECRETS THEY STILL HOLD

sentence_translations.sentence: Dinosaur expert Dr Steve Brusatte continues to investigate the mysteries surrounding these fascinating prehistoric creatures
sentence_translations.translation: 恐龙专家史蒂夫·布鲁萨特博士继续探究这些迷人史前生物所围绕的谜团。

sentence_translations.sentence: I was recently part of a team of palaeontologists that discovered a new dinosaur.
sentence_translations.translation: 我最近加入了一个古生物学家团队，发现了一种新的恐龙。

sentence_translations.sentence: Living in what is now China, the species would have resembled a strange bird.
sentence_translations.translation: 这种物种生活在现在的中国地区，外形类似一种奇特的鸟类。

sentence_translations.sentence: It was about the size of a sheep and covered in feathers, with a sharp beak that it probably used to crack open shellfish.
sentence_translations.translation: 它大约有羊那么大，全身覆盖着羽毛，长着锋利的喙，可能用来敲开贝类。

sentence_translations.sentence: It was given the formal scientific name Tongtianlong, but we called it ‘Mud Dragon’ because its skeleton was discovered in rock that had hardened from ancient mud.
sentence_translations.translation: 它的正式科学名称是‘通天龙’，但我们称它为‘泥浆龙’，因为它的骨骼是在由古代泥浆硬化而成的岩石中发现的。

sentence_translations.sentence: It seems that the creature got trapped in the mud and died.
sentence_translations.translation: 这只生物似乎被困在泥浆中并死亡了。

sentence_translations.sentence: Then its fossil remains were found a few months ago when workmen were excavating a site in order to build a school.
sentence_translations.translation: 随后，几个月前工人们在挖掘一个工地以建造学校时，发现了它的化石遗骸。

sentence_translations.sentence: It is every dinosaur-obsessed child's dearest wish to discover and name a completely new species.
sentence_translations.translation: 每个痴迷恐龙的孩子最渴望的就是发现并命名一个全新的物种。

sentence_translations.sentence: In fact what my colleagues and I did wasn't that unusual.
sentence_translations.translation: 事实上，我和我的同事们所做的并不那么罕见。

sentence_translations.sentence: New dinosaurs are appearing everywhere these days – about 50 each year.
sentence_translations.translation: 如今，新恐龙物种层出不穷——每年大约有50种被发现。

sentence_translations.sentence: And this pace shows no signs of slowing, as different areas continue to open up to fossil hunters and a fresh generation of scientists comes of age.
sentence_translations.translation: 而且这一速度毫无放缓迹象，因为不同地区不断向化石猎人开放，新一代科学家也日渐成熟。

sentence_translations.sentence: Because of this plentiful supply of new fossils, we now know more about dinosaurs than we do about many modern animals.
sentence_translations.translation: 由于新化石的大量涌现，我们现在对恐龙的了解甚至超过了许多现代动物。

sentence_translations.sentence: But there are still many unsolved mysteries.
sentence_translations.translation: 但仍有许多未解之谜。

sentence_translations.sentence: Dinosaurs didn't start out as huge monsters like Tyrannosaurus Rex.
sentence_translations.translation: 恐龙一开始并非像霸王龙那样的巨型怪兽。

sentence_translations.sentence: Instead they evolved from a group of angular, cat-sized reptiles called dinosauromorphs.
sentence_translations.translation: 相反，它们是从一群体型如猫、棱角分明的爬行动物——恐龙形态类——进化而来的。

sentence_translations.sentence: These creatures remained small and rare for millions of years until they developed into dinosaurs.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些生物在数百万年间始终保持体型小且数量稀少，直到它们进化成恐龙。

sentence_translations.sentence: The boundary between dinosauromorphs and dinosaurs is becoming less and less distinct with each new discovery that's made, but what's becoming clear is that it took millions of years for these first dinosaurs to spread around the world, grow to huge sizes and become truly dominant.
sentence_translations.translation: 随着每一项新发现，恐龙形态类与恐龙之间的界限正变得越来越模糊，但逐渐清晰的是，这些最早的恐龙花费了数百万年才扩散到世界各地，长成巨大体型并真正成为统治物种。

sentence_translations.sentence: Some discoveries in the 1970s, like the agile and strangely bird-like Deinonychus, proved that dinosaurs were far more dynamic and intelligent than previously thought.
sentence_translations.translation: 20世纪70年代的一些发现，例如敏捷且异常像鸟类的恐爪龙，证明恐龙比先前认为的要更加活跃、更为聪明。

sentence_translations.sentence: Some palaeontologists even proposed that they were warm-blooded creatures like modern birds with a constant high body temperature that they controlled internally, rather than from warming themselves by lying in the sun.
sentence_translations.translation: 一些古生物学家甚至提出，它们是类似现代鸟类的温血动物，通过内部调节保持恒定的高体温，而非依靠晒太阳来取暖。

sentence_translations.sentence: A few decades later opinions are still mixed.
sentence_translations.translation: 几十年后，观点仍存在分歧。

sentence_translations.sentence: The problem is that dinosaurs can't be observed.
sentence_translations.translation: 问题在于恐龙无法被直接观察。

sentence_translations.sentence: Palaeontologists must rely on studying fossils.
sentence_translations.translation: 古生物学家必须依赖研究化石。

sentence_translations.sentence: Some results are convincing: we know from studying their bones that dinosaurs had rapid growth rates, just like modern, warm-blooded animals.
sentence_translations.translation: 有些结果是令人信服的：通过研究它们的骨骼，我们得知恐龙的生长速度很快，就像现代温血动物一样。

sentence_translations.sentence: Other palaeontologists, however, use the same fossils to suggest that dinosaurs were somewhere between cold-blooded reptiles and warm-blooded birds.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，其他古生物学家利用同样的化石提出，恐龙介于冷血爬行动物和温血鸟类之间。

sentence_translations.sentence: More studies are needed to provide more clarity.
sentence_translations.translation: 需要更多研究来提供更清晰的结论。

sentence_translations.sentence: The discovery of Deinonychus with its long arms, skinny legs, arched neck and big claws on its feet, helped to strengthen the theory that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
sentence_translations.translation: 发现拥有长手臂、细腿、弓形脖子和脚上大爪子的恐爪龙，加强了鸟类由恐龙进化而来的理论。

sentence_translations.sentence: In the late 1990s, the discovery of thousands of feather-covered dinosaurs closed the argument.
sentence_translations.translation: 在20世纪90年代末，数千具覆盖羽毛的恐龙的发现结束了这场争论。

sentence_translations.sentence: But the fossils raised another question: why did feathers first develop in dinosaurs?
sentence_translations.translation: 但这些化石提出了另一个问题：恐龙最初为何会进化出羽毛？

sentence_translations.sentence: They probably originated as simple, hair-like strands - a necessary means of keeping warm.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们可能最初是简单的毛发状纤维——一种必要的保暖方式。

sentence_translations.sentence: Many dinosaurs retained this basic fluffy coat, but in one group the strands modified.
sentence_translations.translation: 许多恐龙保留了这种基本的蓬松外衣，但在一个群体中，这些纤维发生了改变。

sentence_translations.sentence: They grew bigger, started to branch out and changed into feathers like those on modern birds.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们变得更大，开始分叉，并演变成类似于现代鸟类的羽毛。

sentence_translations.sentence: They lined the arms, and sometimes the legs, forming wings.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们排列在手臂上，有时也在腿上，形成了翅膀。

sentence_translations.sentence: These feathers were probably for display: to attract mates or scare off rivals.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些羽毛可能用于展示：以吸引配偶或吓退竞争对手。

sentence_translations.sentence: They appeared in species such as the ostrich-like Ornithomimosaur.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们出现在诸如类似鸵鸟的似鸟龙等物种中。

sentence_translations.sentence: Such creatures were too large to fly.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些生物体型过大，无法飞行。

sentence_translations.sentence: Flight may actually have come about by accident when smaller winged dinosaurs began jumping between trees or leaping in the air, and suddenly found that their wings had aerodynamic properties.
sentence_translations.translation: 飞行实际上可能源于偶然，当较小的有翼恐龙开始在林间跳跃或空中腾跃时，突然发现它们的翅膀具有空气动力学特性。

sentence_translations.sentence: This is one of the most stimulating new notions about dinosaurs and a fascinating area for further investigation.
sentence_translations.translation: 这是关于恐龙最令人振奋的新观念之一，也是一个值得进一步研究的迷人领域。

sentence_translations.sentence: There's something else that these feathers can tell us.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些羽毛还能告诉我们一些别的事情。

sentence_translations.sentence: They allow us to determine what colour dinosaurs were.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们使我们能够确定恐龙的颜色。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you look at modern bird feathers under a microscope, you can see tiny blobs called melanosomes.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你在显微镜下观察现代鸟类的羽毛，你会看到称为黑色素体的小点。

sentence_translations.sentence: These structures contain melanin, one of the main colour-producing pigments in animals.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些结构含有黑色素，这是动物体内产生颜色的主要色素之一。

sentence_translations.sentence: Some are round, others are egg-shaped, etc.
sentence_translations.translation: 有些是圆形的，其他的则是蛋形的，等等。

sentence_translations.sentence: And that's important, because different shapes contain different colour pigments.
sentence_translations.translation: 这很重要，因为不同的形状含有不同的颜色色素。

sentence_translations.sentence: So if you can identify the shape, you can identify the colour.
sentence_translations.translation: 所以如果你能辨别形状，你就能辨别颜色。

sentence_translations.sentence: A few years ago, some palaeontologists realised that you could find melanosomes in particularly well-preserved fossil feathers.
sentence_translations.translation: 几年前，一些古生物学家意识到你可以在保存特别完好的化石羽毛中找到黑色素体。

sentence_translations.sentence: They discovered that different dinosaurs had different melanosomes, which meant they had a variety of colours.
sentence_translations.translation: 他们发现不同的恐龙拥有不同的黑色素体，这意味着它们有各种各样的颜色。

sentence_translations.sentence: Dinosaurs, therefore, probably came in a rainbow of colours - yet another thing that links them to modern birds.
sentence_translations.translation: 因此，恐龙很可能呈现五彩斑斓的颜色——这又是将它们与现代鸟类联系起来的另一个特征。

sentence_translations.sentence: G The most enduring mystery of all, which has been argued about ever since the first dinosaur fossils were found, is ‘Why aren't dinosaurs around today?
sentence_translations.translation: G 最持久的一个谜团，自第一批恐龙化石被发现以来就一直争论不休，就是‘为什么恐龙今天不在了？’

sentence_translations.sentence: Of course, we now know that birds evolved from dinosaurs, so some dinosaurs do continue in a sense.
sentence_translations.translation: 当然，我们现在知道鸟类是从恐龙进化而来的，所以从某种意义上说，一些恐龙确实延续了下来。

sentence_translations.sentence: But there's nothing like a Tyrannosaurus Rex today.
sentence_translations.translation: 但今天再也没有像霸王龙那样的生物了。

sentence_translations.sentence: They dominated the planet for over 150 million years, but suddenly disappeared from the fossil record 66 million years ago.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们统治地球超过1.5亿年，却在6600万年前突然从化石记录中消失。

sentence_translations.sentence: That's when a 10 km-wide asteroid came out of space and struck what is now Mexico, impacting with huge force and unleashing earthquakes, tidal waves, wildfires and hurricane-force winds.
sentence_translations.translation: 那时，一颗宽达10公里的小行星从太空飞来，撞击了现在的墨西哥地区，造成巨大冲击，引发了地震、海啸、野火和飓风级强风。

sentence_translations.sentence: Although palaeontologists still like to argue about what part the asteroid played in the dinosaurs’ extinction, there really isn't much of a mystery left.
sentence_translations.translation: 尽管古生物学家仍喜欢争论小行星在恐龙灭绝中起到了多大作用，但实际上已经没有什么谜团了。

sentence_translations.sentence: The asteroid did it and did it quickly.
sentence_translations.translation: 小行星造成了这一切，而且发生得很快。

sentence_translations.sentence: There are few signs that dinosaurs were struggling before the impact.
sentence_translations.translation: 几乎没有迹象表明恐龙在撞击前已经处于困境。

sentence_translations.sentence: None survived except a few birds and some small furry mammals.
sentence_translations.translation: 除了少数鸟类和一些小型毛茸茸的哺乳动物外，没有其他生物幸存下来。

sentence_translations.sentence: They found themselves in an empty world, and as the planet started to recover, they evolved into new creatures, including the first apes, and so the long journey began to the beginning of humankind.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们发现自己身处一个空旷的世界，随着地球开始恢复，它们进化成了新的生物，包括最早的猿类，由此开启了通向人类起源的漫长旅程。
